messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities.

We need to call the function three times. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter seems to accept a single value or an array? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." It lists options separated by |. For Cafe, it shows "Cafe"[] meaning an array of cafes? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates maybe multiple cafes? But we can pass an array of strings? The type is ambiguous. But likely we need to pass an array of strings for multiple facilities. The function expects a single string? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], so it could be either a string or an array of strings. We'll pass an array of strings for multiple facilities.

Thus:

Call 1: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]

Call 2: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]

Call 3: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to output the results. We'll call the function three times.
